title: Get through governance: security reviews, procurement and change boards
summary: Large organisations protect themselves with reviews and approvals. Learn the routes early, plan their lead times, and treat reviewers as partners.

beginner: Find out which approvals your release needs, such as a security review or a change board.
Ask how long each one usually takes and what it needs from you.
Put the lead times into your plan.
Prepare the paperwork early, with help from people who have done it before.
Meet reviewers before the formal review to hear their concerns.
intermediate: Map every approval route for your product, including buying new tools or suppliers.
Agree standard, lower-risk change types that need lighter approval.
Track approvals as dependencies in the plan.
experienced: Work with governance owners to speed up low-risk approvals.
Use data on delays to argue for lighter routes.
Coach PMs on how to plan for governance.

canDelegateTo.task: Advise on security, legal and procurement requirements

toolExamples.jira: Track each approval as a dependency with a due date.
toolExamples.confluence: Keep a checklist of approvals for your product.

pitfalls: Finding out about a review a week before launch
Repeating the same paperwork from scratch
